properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Shipped-library surface: the Go standard library itself still exports a deprecated RC4 stream cipher and retains RC4 TLS 1.0/1.2 suites for explicit opt-in; they are not offered by default. Changeable here (stdlib source), but removal is a compatibility decision, and the crypto/tls team keeps these behind insecure lists.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go stdlib's own SHA-1 (crypto/sha1, incl. BoringCrypto binding sha1.go:285). Production uses: X.509 subjectKeyId (x509.go:1903 sha1.Sum of SPKI bytes, RFC 5280 method 1), TLS 1.0-1.1 legacy PRF/finished-hash (tls/prf.go:53,166), ECDHE MD5+SHA1 key confirmation (tls/key_agreement.go:109), CBC-suite macSHA1 (tls/cipher_suites.go:423), and the go command's build/action-ID hashing (cmd/go/internal/work/gc.go:622 — non-security cache key). Remaining sites are the sha1 package's own tests and wychepro

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Content-identified RSA-512 public key parsed from pkcs1v15_test.go: it is the classic 512-bit RSA key from the PKCS#1 v1.5 test vectors, embedded as test data in crypto/rsa's own tests. Test material only — never used for production cryptography — but identity is its own bytes, so it is recorded. Any real RSA-512 exposure would be classical breakability; none of the stdlib's production paths use keys this small (FIPS mode rejects <1024, all shipped TLS certs are >=2048 or EC).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go stdlib's CBC mode implementation (crypto/cipher/cbc.go: NewCBCEncrypter/NewCBCDecrypter, the exported BlockMode API). In-tree consumers: TLS 1.0-1.2 CBC cipher suites (TLS layer supplies the HMAC) and legacy RFC 1423 encrypted-PEM (x509/pem_decrypt.go, unauthenticated by design). The rest are the mode's own tests, wycheproof vectors and benchmarks. Malleability is inherent to the mode API; callers must add a MAC.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go standard library's own RSA: crypto/rsa plus the FIPS 140 module (fips140/rsa) and the BoringCrypto shim. The pending sites are its FIPS-enforcement, ACVP and CAST self-test suites — the validation harness for the shipped implementation, which is what ships RSA to every Go program. Shor-vulnerable with no stdlib PQ replacement for RSA signatures yet (ML-DSA exists for new designs); changeable here only as a multi-release stdlib decision.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA-PSS as shipped by the Go standard library: crypto/rsa SignPSS/VerifyPSS, the FIPS module's fips140/rsa/pkcs1v22.go implementation, and the BoringCrypto shim — plus the test suites over them. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; the FIPS-module PSS path is what makes Go 1.28's FIPS 140-3 validation possible. Changeable here as stdlib evolution toward ML-DSA, not per-application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 ENCRYPTION as shipped by Go: crypto/rsa EncryptPKCS1v15/DecryptPKCS1v15, the BoringCrypto shim declarations, and the TLS 1.2 static-RSA key-exchange path (rsaKA suites) which encrypts the premaster secret with PKCS#1 v1.5. The TLS RSA-KEX suites survive only behind explicit Config.CipherSuites opt-in (they sit in InsecureCipherSuites and disabledCipherSuites; the tlsrsakex GODEBUG was removed in Go 1.27 per src/internal/godebugs/table.go:108). Classically risky (Bleichenbacher) a

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA-OAEP as shipped by the Go standard library: crypto/rsa EncryptOAEP/DecryptOAEP, the FIPS module implementation, and the BoringCrypto shim, plus tests. The recommended RSA encryption padding — Shor-vulnerable but still the correct classical choice; ML-KEM-768 is the migration target for new designs. Changeable here only as stdlib evolution.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-224 as shipped-library surface: crypto/sha256's New224, the BoringCrypto shim (goboringcrypto.h, boring/sha.go, boring/hmac.go), and HMAC-SHA2-224 ACVP registration in the FIPS test harness. The stdlib itself uses SHA-224 nowhere security-critical; it ships for interop and NIST ACVP validation (112-bit collision resistance). Quantum-irrelevant (hashes), classically rated C.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 as shipped: the stdlib's internal/poly1305 implementation, consumed by ChaCha20-Poly1305 (TLS, QUIC) and HPKE's AEAD (crypto/hpke/aead.go). Sound AEAD component; quantum-irrelevant (symmetric).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go stdlib's stream-mode implementations (crypto/cipher NewCTR/NewCFBEncrypter/NewCFBDecrypter/NewOFB) with their tests, fuzz corpus and examples. One production consumer: crypto/tls/ticket.go:344,394 encrypts/decrypts TLS session tickets with AES-CTR inside an encrypt-then-MAC construction (keyed HMAC over the ticket state), so the unauthenticated-mode concern is addressed by that caller.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CMAC/GMAC inside the FIPS 140 module: fips140/aes/gcm/cmac.go implements CMAC (SP 800-38B) and ctrkdf.go the CMAC-based counter-mode KDF (SP 800-108) used to derive AES-GCM subkeys; the GHASH-based GMAC round out the GCM machinery. NIST-required constructions for the FIPS validation; sound.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The stdlib's own ECDH: crypto/ecdh (X25519, X448, P-256/384/521 via nistec), used by TLS 1.3 key shares (including the classical half of X25519MLKEM768) and by applications. Shor-vulnerable key agreement — the reason the hybrid ML-KEM groups exist; standalone ECDH use remains retroactively breakable. Changeable here: the hybrid migration is already shipped for TLS; the raw ECDH API stays classical.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The stdlib's own ECDSA: crypto/ecdsa with the FIPS 140 module implementation (deterministic + hedged nonce per FIPS 186-5), used by x509, TLS, and applications; P-256/384/521. Shor-vulnerable signatures — the classic-past deadline problem; ML-DSA is shipped in parallel for new designs and hybrid certificates. Changeable here as stdlib evolution.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The stdlib's own Ed25519: crypto/ed25519 (including Ed25519ph and Ed25519ctx variants per the sites' selector switches), consumed by x509, TLS and applications. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; migration path ML-DSA. Nonce handling is deterministic (RFC 8032), avoiding the ECDSA nonce-reuse class.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The tree's TLS session posture on Go 1.28 defaults: 247 sites where the stdlib's own code and tools (cmd/go web/vcweb fetchers, misc/ios, httptest-armed tests across net/http, crypto/tls) open TLS sessions with default configuration. Default settings: minimum TLS 1.2, maximum TLS 1.3, and X25519MLKEM768 hybrid post-quantum key exchange offered by default since Go 1.24 (GODEBUG tlsmlkem, src/internal/godebugs/table.go:66; CurvePreferences docs, crypto/tls/common.go:807-821). Sessions are therefor

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 as shipped: crypto/ecdh's X25519 and its use as the classical half of the default X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group in TLS 1.3. Standalone X25519 key agreement is Shor-vulnerable; in the hybrid it is defense-in-depth alongside ML-KEM-768. Sites: implementation, nistec-free field arithmetic, wycheproof vectors, TLS group code, tests.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) as shipped: the stdlib's nistec P-256 implementation used by crypto/ecdsa, crypto/ecdh, x509, TLS (including the SecP256r1MLKEM768 hybrid group's classical half). Shor-vulnerable; the FIPS module's nistec is the validated implementation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The tree's constant-time comparison infrastructure — the positive control that makes the non-constant-time object noise: crypto/subtle's ConstantTimeCompare, hmac.Equal, the GCM tag verification (cipher/gcm.go), ECDH shared-secret checks (ecdh.go). These are the sites where MACs and digests ARE compared in constant time. Sound.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.2 ships and remains the default minimum version of crypto/tls. Sites: the FIPS 140 service indicator for TLSv1.2-SHA2-256 (fips140/tls12/cast.go), httptest's VersionTLS12 pin (shipped test utility), a net/http client test pinning MaxVersion, and the CAST test. TLS 1.2 sessions use classical ECDHE only — hybrid PQ groups are TLS 1.3-only — so peers that actually negotiate 1.2 get retroactively-breakable key exchange; the Go default maximum is 1.3, which mitigates this for modern peers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TLS 1.3 floors and the FIPS service indicator for TLSv1.3-SHA2-256: the version that carries the hybrid PQ key-share groups. Sites: the fips140 CAST declaration, the stdlib's own HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 tests pinning MinVersion = TLS 1.3, and an openssl output-parsing constant. The right posture pin; nothing weak here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The shipped pinning mechanism of Go's crypto/tls: Config.VerifyPeerCertificate is the standard hook applications use for certificate or public-key pinning. common.go:1024 is the Config.Clone plumbing; the other two sites are the TLS package's own tests exercising the callback. The stdlib itself pins nothing — applications opt in. Posture control API, quantum-relevant only in that pinned classical keys will need rotation alongside ML-DSA migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The fips140test browser-bridge harness opens real TLS sessions on default settings (role labels "go-https-client") to validate the FIPS 140 module's TLS stack interop. Default settings for this Go version offer X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange (GODEBUG tlsmlkem on since Go 1.24), so these sessions are not purely classical.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go stdlib's NIST P-384/P-521: nistec implementations under crypto/internal/nistec, exposed through crypto/ecdh (P384()/P521()), crypto/ecdsa, crypto/elliptic and crypto/tls (classical groups in the default curve preferences). Quantum-vulnerable key-agreement/signature curves: harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to recorded P-384/P-521 ECDH traffic. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X448 genuinely ships in crypto/ecdh (ecdh.X448(), the Curve448 field arithmetic and its Wycheproof vectors). NOTE: most pending sites are identifier collisions — fiat-crypto-GENERATED limb variables named x448 in p384_fiat64.go/p521_fiat64.go ("var x448 uint64") — which are not X448 uses; the Wycheproof JWK schema constants accompany real shipped X448 vector runs. Shor-vulnerable key agreement, opt-in, rarely used; migration ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The stdlib's own ML-DSA (FIPS 204): crypto/ml-dsa implements ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87, wired into x509 (composite/hybrid certificate support), TLS, and the FIPS 140 module; 705 sites are implementation, ACVP/CAST validation and tests. This IS the post-quantum signature migration target — quantum-safe; recorded so the CBOM shows which parameter sets ship (all three, not just the 65 default).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The stdlib's own ML-KEM (FIPS 203): crypto/mlkem implements ML-KEM-512/768/1024; it powers the default X25519MLKEM768 and SecP256r1MLKEM768 TLS 1.3 groups (on by default since Go 1.24) and HPKE's ML-KEM KEMs (crypto/hpke/kem.go). This is the harvest-now-decrypt-later countermeasure already shipped; recording that all three parameter sets are available, not just 768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go stdlib's GCM (crypto/cipher/gcm.go, internal fips140 AES-GCM) — the AEAD used by TLS 1.2 ECDHE suites, TLS 1.3 and HPKE. Quantum-safe symmetric primitive; the tree exercises both AES-128 and AES-256 (AES-128 floor is 64-bit PQ security under Grover; AES-256 preferred where PQ margin matters).

properties.value: AES-128 as shipped: the stdlib's crypto/aes (hardware AES-NI/ARMv8 paths plus the FIPS 140 module's AES) — key size matters for the record: 128-bit here, quantum-relevant only via Grover halving to 64-bit effective, still fine for the medium term; used across TLS, cipher modes, x509, tests.
